The prior sweep assigned the measurement runner to native `claude plugin eval`. This is therefore proposed as the missing upstream case set with deterministic verifiers, not as a second runner. SkillsBench ships 87 tasks across 8 domains under a paired no-Skills/curated-Skills protocol. Each task carries environment/skills, oracle/solve.sh and verifier/test.sh. Its README injects any skill directory with `--skill-mode with-skill --skills-dir <dir>` and runs locally with `--sandbox docker`. BenchFlow drives the native Claude Code CLI (`--agent claude` after `claude auth login`) and the Codex CLI (`--agent codex` after `codex login`) on existing subscriptions. The winners' installed skill folders can therefore run against a frozen, verifier-graded task set with no new credentials. Its paper also finds that focused skills with at most three modules beat larger or exhaustive bundles. That is the requirement's no-whole-catalog claim, stated as a testable hypothesis. proposed.demonstrated_gap: The native winners (Claude Code workers plus Worktrunk) have four gaps: no executed head-to-head, no replay-determinism check, no enforced per-task write allowlist, and an unresolved accounting gap. Bernstein's documented design targets exactly those frozen cases. After one decomposition call, scheduling is plain Python with no model in the loop. Every run writes a replay journal, and `bernstein replay latest --verify` recomputes the journal head. Each coding task gets its own git worktree behind merge gates. A task's owned_files become a write allowlist, enforced by a PreToolUse hook that refuses out-of-scope writes and a Stop hook that refuses to end the turn while required verification fails; both hooks are rendered into capable agent adapters. The task lifecycle has CANCELLED, ORPHANED (agent crashed mid-task, awaits crash recovery) and PENDING_APPROVAL (human approval before merge). The 'assisted' graduation stage requires explicit human approval for each task merge. Stop and drain come in graceful and force forms, and workflow resume works from `.sdd/runs/<run_id>/` checkpoints. Token progress is tracked per agent. It installs locally with uv (Python >=3.12), keeps state in files and needs no SaaS. Caveats recorded as facts: the README says 'solo maintained'. The project's own automation self-merges when CI is green, which is consistent with 2385 default-branch commits since 2026-07-01, the latest by renovate[bot]. The repo has published 11 advisories (9 high), among them the 2026-08-14 task-JWT and cross-tenant fixes. Every capability claim is upstream self-description: the demo is a mock-agent run, and no independent benchmark was found.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Freeze one representative coding task. Run it under native Claude Code Workflow (isolation: worktree, Worktrunk 0.80.0) and under Bernstein 3.20.0: install with `uv tool install bernstein==3.20.0`, do a zero-token dry pass with the `mock` adapter, then run the Claude Code adapter at the same model and effort in the 'assisted' stage. Bernstein earns adoption only if it passes every frozen case: (1) `bernstein stop` and a force stop mid-run leave each owned worktree's edits and the journal intact; (2) `bernstein replay latest --verify` reproduces the journal and task-graph hash; (3) after retry or model re-route, the patch and gate logs of a seeded failing attempt can still be retrieved; (4) no merge lands before PENDING_APPROVAL is cleared; (5) the owned_files hook gate refuses a planted out-of-scope write. Its per-agent token totals must also reconcile with provider-reported usage, at complete usage no worse than the native run. If any case fails, or native Workflow passes the same cases at lower complete usage, Bernstein drops to keep_but_compare or is refuted.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The overturn condition names approval waits and effect recovery beyond native workers, and Paperclip's control plane documents both. It offers atomic task checkout with execution locks and a DB-backed heartbeat wakeup queue whose recovery 'handles orphaned runs automatically'. Execution workspaces are isolated git worktrees. Board approval workflows and execution policies add review and approval stages, and agents can be paused, resumed or terminated. Token and cost tracking runs by agent, issue, provider and model, with budget hard-stops. None of this is provided durably across a host restart by native workers, where hard crash and reboot recovery is unqualified. It is not a trial now for four reasons: no real task yet needs approval waits; the stack is heavy (installer requires Node.js >=24.11 and can install a background service); how it derives usage is unverified, so it may inherit the same stream-derived deduplication gap; and the repo has 12 published advisories, 5 of them critical. The latest (2026-07-22) was a drive-by RCE against local instances via DNS rebinding, affecting versions below 0.3.1.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: A real task needs an approval wait or must survive a host restart. On the frozen task, Paperclip must meet all of the following: run a release at or after the GHSA-x8hx-rhr2-9rf7 fix, bound to loopback; recover the orphaned run after kill -9 of the server and a host reboot, without duplicate effects; hold the merge until a board approval is given; keep the failed run's workspace; and report token totals that reconcile with provider-reported usage. If native Workflow fails the same restart and approval cases while Paperclip passes, the comparison overturns.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: This is the only shortlisted candidate built for durable multi-host delegation, which the overturn condition names. A Go backend with PostgreSQL 17 connects to a local agent daemon on each machine, and the daemon spawns Claude Code, Codex and other CLIs. Work can therefore route across the WSL workstation and the Macs while code stays on each host. The README documents review gates ('Work lands in review, not in main'), an execution log that replays every tool call, command and error, per-run and per-agent usage analytics, and retries and timeouts where failed runs either retry or stop and report why. It is not a trial now for four reasons: no real task yet needs multi-host state; self-hosting pulls GHCR images and requires Docker; the README does not state per-task worktree isolation; and daily anonymous deployment telemetry is on unless DO_NOT_TRACK=1. proposed.demonstrated_gap: After delegation, native workers do not follow a worker's pull request. AO's local daemon tracks each worker's own branch and worktree, its pull request, CI, review state and merge conflicts, and it returns actionable failures and review comments to the worker that owns the work. That is integrate-after-review with routing back to the owner. Its CLI docs cover a headless path: `ao start` runs the daemon in the background, alongside `ao spawn` and `ao session kill/restore/resume-agent`. State lives in SQLite, and the daemon binds only to 127.0.0.1. `ao session switch-agent` moves a worker between Claude Code and Codex while preserving the session and worktree. It is kept for comparison rather than trial for three reasons: the README install path is desktop downloads, and the standalone `ao` binary is built from a source checkout; telemetry sends the signed-in GitHub username on session start unless telemetry is turned off; and its review loop depends on a forge PR flow. The 2026-09-26 refutation named a different repository, so this project was never adjudicated.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Deliver the frozen task through a PR seeded with a CI failure and a review comment. With a headless `ao start` daemon, AO must route both back to the owning worker, keep that worker's branch and worktree across `ao session kill` and `restore`, and switch the worker between Claude Code and Codex without losing edits, all with complete usage recorded. It overturns the native path if native workers need manual routing to reach the same outcome at equal or higher complete usage.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Gas City composes with Beads, which is already a conditional alternative pinned at 1.3.0, and it targets durable state. proposed.demonstrated_gap:
The winners supply no VM boundary, no resource caps and no hostile-workload qualification (open gap 5). srt's network evidence covers only temporary IPv4 loopback HTTP (open gap 1). BoxLite v0.10.4 runs each box as a hardware-virtualized VM (KVM / Hypervisor.framework) inside an OS sandbox (seccomp / sandbox-exec), with CPU/memory/resource limits, an allow_net egress allowlist and host-side secret injection (README Features). Its narrower discriminators over the other no-credential local VM candidates are twofold. First, among those candidates only its README lists a Windows (WSL2) x86_64 row ('WSL2 with KVM support, user in kvm group'); microsandbox and Brig document Linux and macOS but no WSL2 row. Second, it documents a seccomp/sandbox-exec layer around the VM. All four published advisories are fixed at v0.10.4:
- Two critical advisories were patched in 0.9.0.
- High GHSA-c7v3 (allow_net Host/SNI versus dialed-IP bypass) and medium GHSA-xjhv (exec timeout bypass) are both listed without a patched version. A code read at the tag (not executed) shows both fixed. Hostname-authorized egress now dials the name through host-side resolution and discards the guest's destination IP (fix commits #1330 2026-08-25 and #1495 2026-09-18). Exec timeouts escalate from SIGTERM to SIGKILL.

Four advisories in 2026, including the same allowlist-bypass class as microsandbox's GHSA-3mpp, are a maintenance fact the trial must probe. Trial precondition, an operator host change and not a refutation: this host's /dev/kvm is crw-rw---- root:systemd-resolve and the user is not in that group, so the documented kvm-group step alone will not grant access.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
A bounded native trial of BoxLite v0.10.4 against srt 0.0.77, first on linux-wsl2 and then on macOS arm64, reusing the srt receipt fixtures:
1. Filesystem permit/deny, including the overlapping denied read/write path (open gap 4).
2. Network egress with TLS, DNS, IPv6 and a remote host.
3. A Host/SNI-allowlisted name sent to a non-matching IP.
4. An allowlisted name that resolves to loopback, 169.254.169.254 or private address space, including a DNS-rebinding case. This is an untested boundary: at v0.10.4 the link-local check reads the guest-chosen address, and whether the host-side resolution in egress_dialer.go filters such results was not read.
5. A memory hog and a CPU hog that must be capped, and an exec timeout that must kill a process that ignores SIGTERM.
6. No residual processes, mounts, QCOW2 disks or state directories after removal.

BoxLite is adopted for untrusted workloads only if, on both hosts, it enforces every axis srt enforces plus resource caps, with clean teardown. Any reproduced allowlist bypass, uncapped hog or leftover state refutes it.

The recorded macOS VM alternative, apple/container 1.4.1, is Mac-only and requires macOS 26 according to the 2026-09-26 sweep record (not re-verified here). Lima (Apache-2.0, v2.2.0 released 2026-07-21, v2.3.0-beta.0 released 2026-09-01) is a mature full-VM path. Its AI-agent guide recommends mounting only the project directory ('limactl start --mount-only .:w', read-only without ':w'). The same guide documents no egress allowlist and no resource-cap recipe, so network and resource enforcement would still need srt or a guest firewall. A full VM is also heavier than the microVM candidates.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
The 2026-09-26 not_adopted label rested on the PolyForm Noncommercial license alone ('says nothing about its code-graph quality'). Under the current rules a license is information only, so that rejection is void and the repository needs a merit label.

On merit it is the most complete static-graph challenger to codebase-memory-mcp, which is the same class and already a conditional alternative:
- 19 MCP tools, including:
  - context: categorized references
  - impact: blast radius with depth grouping and confidence
  - trace: shortest call path
  - detect_changes: git diff to affected processes
  - rename: graph plus text search
  - read_file (sliced) and grep
- Very active: a default-branch commit on 2026-09-28 tightens Python receiver resolution, the stable release is v1.6.12, and v1.6.13 release candidates run up to rc.53.

The only outside measurement is by a competitor (pixel PR #190: grep-derived ground truth, 4 repos, 3 languages). For GitNexus 1.6.12 it reports:
- Impact recall 0.84 against pixel's 0.86 on 29 cases.
- p50 latency 432 ms and 11.0 KB answers.
- About 19,700 always-on tokens (17 MCP schemas plus an injected block). Deferred tool discovery cuts the schema share but not the injected instruction block.

Why not targeted:
- No evidence that it beats codebase-memory-mcp, or Serena's language-server references, on reference correctness.
- 'gitnexus analyze' also installs skills, registers Claude Code hooks and writes AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. That conflicts with this repo's shared-config rule, so any trial must run in a scratch checkout.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
It is new to the layer (not in known_repositories), and it works differently from the current winners:
- A tree-sitter graph over 81 languages, plus 88 framework integrations that add semantic edges (routes, components, ORM relations, migrations, events). Neither Serena's language servers nor the current graph alternatives model these edges.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The winners leave OCR, inferred layouts and arbitrary filings unqualified: poppler acceptance covers only born-digital Latin pages with explicit table geometry, and markitdown's PDF/Office extras are unestablished. MinerU 4.0.0 (2026-09-16) is a major rebuild with four parsing tiers. The flash tier reads native PDF text with no models. The basic tier runs ONNX OCR and table models on CPU. The standard and advanced tiers add a VLM; they need 8 GB+ VRAM through PyTorch plus vLLM on NVIDIA, and use PyTorch plus llama.cpp on Apple Silicon. MinerU 4 parses Office, EPUB, HTML and CSV natively. It also ships a local library (find/search/read/show/watch/scan) with stable locators of the form doc:{id}/tier:{tier}/page:{page}/block:{block}, which return the original page or block for citation. No winner provides that for PDFs or Office files. Limits: its README says it is not a RAG framework or vector database, and that search covers only content MinerU has already indexed. The search method is undocumented, so MinerU complements qmd rather than replacing it. No independent benchmark covers 4.0. OmniDocBench is run by opendatalab, MinerU's own organisation; it scores the MinerU2.5-Pro VLM at 95.75 and MinerU-Pipeline at 86.47, and the 4.0 mapping from tier to model is unverified. proposed.demonstrated_gap: The winners split the work. MarkItDown is qualified only for HTML conversion (open_gaps leaves its PDF/Office extras unestablished), and Poppler covers only designed born-digital Latin pages, with no OCR or inferred layout. Xberg was renamed from kreuzberg-dev/kreuzberg; its README calls it 'the next iteration of Kreuzberg ... under a fresh v1 line'. It is one MIT-licensed Rust engine with Python bindings, a CLI and an MCP server (`xberg mcp --transport stdio`, 9 tools). It converts PDF, Office and image files to Markdown with OCR (Tesseract, PaddleOCR on ONNX Runtime, Candle or VLM), ML layout models (PP-DocLayout-V3, RT-DETR) and table structure (TATR, SLANet), on CPU by default. So one component targets both unqualified gaps. v1.3.0 (2026-09-29) sends pages whose text-layer character map is unusable to Tesseract PSM 6 and records the mode in metadata.additional.ocr_page_segmentation_modes. Risks to test rather than assume: (a) the sources I read do not identify the default 'native' PDF backend; pdfium is opt-in and libpdfium is not bundled. (b) Automatic OCR fallback could replace text-layer bodies. (c) Churn is high: the v1 line began at v1.0.0 on 2026-07-28 and has shipped about 40 release tags since, including v1.2.0 to v1.3.0 in 15 days, so pin v1.3.0 / commit 1409e7be4b. Xberg is open-core: Pro and Enterprise are commercial, and only the MIT engine is in scope. The xberg.io/benchmarks claims are vendor-authored and were not read.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Step 1: re-run the retained inputs the winners were accepted on, meaning the HTML sources MarkItDown converted and the designed born-digital PDFs Poppler handled. Xberg v1.3.0 (native backend, then pdfium) must match on exact-phrase source-body recall against both the installed MarkItDown winner (the layer input pins it inconsistently: winners[] says 0.1.7, components_vs_upstream says 0.1.8) and Poppler 26.09.0 pdftotext. It must also show zero pages where automatic OCR replaced a usable text layer, checked in metadata.additional.ocr_page_segmentation_modes. Step 2: on a sealed held-out set of filings, multi-column pages, bordered and borderless tables, scanned pages and Office files, it must beat both on table TEDS, reading order and OCR text accuracy, with acceptable repeated end-to-end latency. Failing step 1 or losing step 2 keeps Poppler plus MarkItDown.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: A model-free, CPU-only PDF-to-Markdown arm for Poppler's unqualified inferred-layout pages and MarkItDown's unestablished PDF path. It rebuilds reading order across multi-column pages, emits GFM or HTML tables, chunks by page with metadata, and OCRs only the regions that need it (Tesseract through PyMuPDF, or rapidocr_onnxruntime; with neither installed, OCR is off with a warning). proposed.demonstrated_gap: A maintained GitHub-hosted model for the VLM-OCR class this layer lacks. The 09-26 return found GLM-OCR, dots.ocr and DeepSeek-OCR-2 stale and OvisOCR2 HF-only, and this round confirms dots.ocr and dots.mocr are stale. Logics-Parsing-V3 (released 2026-09-22) is a 0.8B vision-language model that parses multi-page documents. It carries a structural state across pages to merge cross-page tables, keep text continuous and recover the heading hierarchy, and writes markdown.md, hierarchy.md, raw_output.dsl and result.json. That targets the unqualified OCR, inferred-layout and arbitrary-filing gaps: Poppler has no OCR, and cross-page tables are common in filings. At 0.8B it fits the RTX 4090. Every score is self-reported: the highest Overall on MPDocBench and on a self-constructed MPDocBench-Long, 'competitive' results on OmniDocBench v1.6, and 1.39 s/page against OvisOCR2 1.40, Unlimited-OCR 1.72 and MinerU2.5-Pro 3.35 on unspecified hardware. proposed.demonstrated_gap: The layer has no measured retrieval quality (open gap: one real question plus four upstream examples establish compatibility only). Semble ships a pinned, runnable cross-tool code-search harness: ~1,250 NL queries over 63 repos pinned by revision in repos.json, 19 languages, split semantic 711 / architecture 343 / symbol 204. On it, semble runs CPU-only with the 16M-param static Model2Vec potion-code-16M-v2 plus BM25, fuses them by RRF and applies a code-aware reranker. It reports NDCG@10 0.854 with a 306 ms cold index and 0.91 ms warm query p50, against 0.839 for the 137M CodeRankEmbed and 0.630 for codebase-memory-mcp (already installed here). SocratiCode documents dense + BM25 RRF-fused search over Qdrant, and no rerank stage was found in its README. Semble's own ablation credits its reranker with most of its gain (BM25 0.675->0.834, potion 0.650->0.821, hybrid 0.854). Semble needs neither a GPU embedding service nor a vector-DB service. Its index is a rebuildable cache (~/.cache/semble on Linux, ~/Library/Caches/semble on macOS, overridable with SEMBLE_CACHE_LOCATION), which sidesteps SocratiCode's unestablished watcher/index recovery and offers a candidate lane for macOS, where all three winners are untested (arm64 wheels not checked). CAVEATS: this is a vendor benchmark. Claude Sonnet 4.6 generated the queries and relevance labels and also judged label quality. The ablations are reported on the same queries, with no held-out split documented. SocratiCode and Nemotron-3-Embed-1B are absent from the table. SEMBLE_MODEL_NAME accepts only Model2Vec-compatible models, so adoption would replace the requirement's 'compatible embedding service' clause: an architecture decision, not a configuration option.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run the pinned Semble harness (benchmarks.run_benchmark plus baselines) on the workstation CPU and one M5 Pro, add SocratiCode 1.16.0 + Qdrant 1.19.1 + Nemotron-3-Embed-1B/vLLM over the same queries, and score every system on the layer's frozen project question set with expected source spans. If SocratiCode's file-level NDCG@10 and hit@k on the frozen set are equal to or above semble's (paired bootstrap 95% CI of the difference not below 0), semble stays a complement at most. If semble matches or beats it on the frozen set with lower index time, lower RSS and no service state to restore, semble becomes the replacement (or CPU/macOS-lane) candidate.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Late-interaction (multi-vector) retrieval carries the only score reported above semble's on the same public harness. LightOn reports NDCG@10 0.859 for LateOn-Code (137M) and 0.846 for LateOn-Code-edge (17M) against semble 0.853, run on an H100 at FP32. Semble's own CPU-only run lists ColGREP at 0.693 (5.4 s index, 122 ms query p50; --code-only except bash repos). This 0.15 conflict is unresolved: both figures are vendor-reported under different hardware, precision, flags and possibly versions, so only a native reproduction decides it. The current stack runs single-vector dense Nemotron-3-Embed-1B + BM25 with no quality measurement. ColGREP is one Rust binary with v1.7.0 release builds for aarch64-apple-darwin and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, so it fits both hosts. It offers hybrid regex + semantic queries and a memory-mapped PLAID index with incremental updates (only changed files are re-encoded), stored outside the project (~/.local/share/colgrep/indices, XDG_DATA_HOME honored). It needs no vector-DB service or embedding server. Reproducing the GPU configuration depends on a CUDA-enabled build (not verified). Default-branch activity is lower (last commit 2026-08-18); that is recorded as a fact, not a reason to exclude.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The closest same-architecture alternative with fewer stateful services. It uses tree-sitter AST chunks, `ccc index` build-or-update, a background daemon (`ccc daemon`), CLI or MCP serving (`ccc mcp`), `ccc doctor` index-health diagnostics and `ccc reset`. Instead of a Qdrant service it uses embedded per-project databases: cocoindex.db and target_sqlite.db under <project>/.cocoindex_code/, relocatable with COCOINDEX_CODE_DB_PATH_MAPPING. Its README documents OpenAI-compatible endpoints including vLLM via LiteLLM's openai/ prefix and OPENAI_BASE_URL, so it could reuse the existing Nemotron endpoint unchanged. That targets the lifecycle half of the requirement (Qdrant state plus SocratiCode's unestablished watcher recovery) without touching the embedding service. It has no retrieval-quality evidence: it is absent from Semble's benchmarked and excluded methods, and its README offers only a 70% token-saving claim. No quality gap is demonstrated yet.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: TOO NEW TO ASSESS (<90 days): created 2026-07-13, one commit and no release. This is an additional MTEB-based code-retrieval harness from authors who are not behind any of the retrieval tools proposed here. The paper (arXiv 2606.11864 v3, accepted to EMNLP 2026 Main) reports over 180K queries and 106K broader-context relevance labels across three levels: code understanding (nine Level-1 tasks via revision-pinned MTEB loaders plus CLARC/CPRet), issue-to-edit localization from SWE-bench-series instances, and broader-context retrieval. The ecosystem already catalogs MTEB and Agent Retrieval Bench (345 positive file-level samples). What CORE-Bench adds is scale, for tighter confidence intervals, and SWE-bench-derived localization. The Semble bench is vendor-generated and not held out for semble. CORE-Bench scores the embedding model through run_mteb.py (e.g. Nemotron-3-Embed-1B vs Qwen3-Embedding or code-specialized models), not the full SocratiCode chunking-plus-hybrid pipeline. Per the abstract, representative embedding models drop sharply from traditional code search to agentic repository retrieval. Unverified: several author names appear to match the Qwen3-Embedding report, and the harness's reference model is Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, so treat Qwen results with care.

If Nemotron then ranks below another open model by more than the run-to-run spread, reopen the embedding choice. Drop it if the single-commit toolkit cannot run the pinned model without local patches.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The only challenger with a matched harness result against the control. On the preregistered LongMemEval-S retrieval harness (Mac, n = 470, descriptive under A15.2), agentmemory with local all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (arm D2) scored recall_all@5 0.821. ai-memory's production embedder with the reranker off (C3) scored 0.570 and plain BM25 scored 0.747, so the retained control trails a lexical baseline. One plugin directory serves both Codex and Claude Code. On Codex it registers six lifecycle hooks: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact and Stop. It also provides /forget with a governance delete, /handoff, an audit endpoint and JSON export/import with merge, replace or skip, which map onto capture, deletion, handoff and recovery. Two things remain unmeasured: its standing against C4 (ai-memory with its LLM reranker) and its shipped hook capture path (D2h). Risk facts: 1) Two consecutive releases fixed scope-isolation security defects. v0.9.27 (2026-06-07) fixed AGENTMEMORY_AGENT_SCOPE=isolated not being enforced on search and recall. v0.9.28 (2026-07-19) closed a cross-agent leak via /agentmemory/context. 2) No release has shipped since v0.9.29 (2026-08-16). 3) The default branch has 39 commits since 2026-07-01, lower activity that is recorded, not excluded. 4) The runtime depends on the iii engine. 5) Codex Desktop does not dispatch plugin hooks (openai/codex#16430, as cited by the README), so Codex capture there needs the ~/.codex/hooks.json workaround.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: A local verbatim memory with a deterministic, zero-LLM write path, auto-save hooks for Claude Code and Codex CLI, and local backends (ChromaDB by default, or sqlite_exact). Its committed per-question LongMemEval results, re-scored by this repository, give recall_all@5 0.857 raw (470 questions) and 0.887 hybrid v4 (424 held-out, tuned on LongMemEval). Both are far above C3 at 0.570, but neither has been reproduced here. Verification boundary: raw mode bypasses the palace code that the hooks write through, and third-party runs put the palace modes at 89.4% and 84.2% recall_any. The independent analysis in arXiv 2604.21284 attributes the headline to verbatim storage plus ChromaDB's default all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and reports end-to-end LongMemEval QA of about 67.2%. So the shipped path and its usefulness are unproven. Lifecycle facts: v3.9.0 purges stale closets when a drawer is updated or deleted, and v3.8.0 stopped sync --apply from deleting drawers whose source it could not reach. Advisory GHSA-7qpw-4fjh-7g82 (medium, 2026-09-15) reports that the remote MCP read-only mode can be bypassed.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: On WSL2, reproduce in the same harness both the raw arm and the palace path that the Claude Code and Codex hooks actually write, against C3 and C4, under the +5 pp Holm replacement rule. Then run memory-lane acceptance: a scoped decision with cross-scope negatives, a deleted drawer that stays absent after re-mine and sync, and a restore onto an isolated store. It is refuted if the hook-written palace path does not beat C4, even when raw mode does.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: TOO NEW TO ASSESS (<90 days): created 2026-07-14, so the 90-day maintenance rule cannot score it yet (2,075 default-branch commits since creation; v0.21.3 on 2026-09-27). It targets two recorded gaps of the winner. ai-memory captures sanitized assistant excerpts capped at 2,000 bytes and has Claude prompt capture opted out. deja instead indexes the complete native Claude Code and Codex CLI transcripts with no capture step, no model and no server, so it adds no second capture owner. Both clients are fully supported: MCP recall, auto-recall, skill, command, resume and handoff. Deletion and privacy: `deja forget` keeps sessions dropped across rebuilds (tombstones, v0.21.2); credentials are redacted at index time; `deja secrets --scrub` rewrites transcripts that still hold them. Decisions and handoffs: `deja promote --state rejected|accepted` marks superseded decisions, and `deja handoff --to codex` moves work between clients. Recovery: the index rebuilds from the native stores, and `deja sync ssh` copies it between machines with no cloud. It also commits its LongMemEval-S and LoCoMo run files and a driver that scores any system's ranking file, which gives a ready matched-scoring path. Risk facts: advisory GHSA-x885-hr98-9crg (medium, 2026-07-18) reports that agent config backups could expose credentials and crafted session IDs could alter resume commands. The previous sweep's verifier found a single npm maintainer with no provenance and a Scorecard Code-Review score of 0/10.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run a read-only trial over the existing transcripts on WSL2. Build a question set from this repository's recorded decisions and handoffs across Claude and Codex sessions. Score deja (lexical, embeddings off) against ai-memory C3 and C4 on that set, and on LongMemEval-S through its -score driver, under the +5 pp Holm rule. Plant a credential and a forgotten session, rebuild the index, and confirm both stay absent. It is refuted if recall does not beat C4, if a forgotten session reappears after the rebuild, or if the planted credential survives in the index.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: It has the strongest end-to-end QA evidence among local-capable candidates, and its active lifecycle work targets two of the winner's open gaps: deletion covered only current search results, and restore and reindex were never run. v0.10.1 (2026-09-21) deletes a bank's stored files with the bank, scopes file keys to the tenant, and reports deleted_count from bulk deletes. v0.9.1 round-trips every bank config field through export and import. v0.8.6 fixed backup-restore schema compatibility. Memory banks are strictly isolated, Memory Defense can redact or block secrets and PII at retain, and ingestion from Claude Code and Codex CLI is automatic. It supports Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 through Docker, pip or embedded pg0. Its quality figure is vendor-run: 94.6% on LongMemEval in single-query mode on its AMB harness (blog, 2026-03-23). The README claims independent reproduction by Virginia Tech and The Washington Post, which this sweep did not verify. The same post says naive full-context runs now score competitively on LongMemEval. Retain runs an LLM over every ingested item, so a matched run carries provider usage that the retrieval-only harness does not yet measure. That cost is why it is keep_but_compare rather than a trial now.

INCUMBENCY: ai-memory's standing rests on incumbency and lifecycle coverage, not on measured recall.
- catalogs/landscape/foundation.json (origin/main, line 1905) calls it "retained as the production control, not as a measured best".
- The committed memory-stack-20260925 experiment measured its production configuration C3 at recall_all@5 0.570. That is below plain BM25 (0.747), dense-qwen3 (0.753) and agentmemory+MiniLM (0.821). Sources: experiment.json lines 961 and 1023; docs/decisions/2026-09-27-mac-single-writer-staged.md line 48; memory-stack-20260925.json line 944. The run was Mac-only, descriptive and retrieval-only, and C4 (reranker on) was never run.
- memory-stack-20260925.json line 65 also records that its binary provenance conflicts with the official-artifact rule.
- So open_gaps[0] ("No matched semantic-recall ... benchmark ... exists") is out of date. A matched retrieval benchmark exists. What is missing is C4, a WSL2 replication and any usefulness measure.

NATIVE ARMS (possible duplicate memory owners):
- Claude Code auto memory is on by default and stored per project under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory).
- Claude Code 2.1.284 (2026-09-28) neutralizes invisible characters and markup-imitating tags in MEMORY.md and recalled notes. 2.1.275 added viewing, editing and deleting saved memories in VS Code. Both come from the anthropics/claude-code CHANGELOG.
- Claude sessions therefore run two memory owners, auto memory and ai-memory.
- Codex features.memories stays off by default (https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference), with memories.use_memories and memories.disable_on_external_context controls.
- Codex rust-v0.158.0 (2026-09-28) only stabilized memory dual-write tests (#47817). The layer's Codex pin 0.157.1 is behind 0.158.0.

Maintenance was then established by the task's REST route (commits?since=2026-07-01T00:00:00Z&per_page=1) for every proposed repository, every winner, exa-mcp-server and jina-ai/reader.

WINNER HEALTH.
(1) vercel-labs/agent-browser: pin 0.38.1 equals the latest release, v0.38.1 (2026-09-16). Latest main commit d01253d9db28 on 2026-09-22 (83 since 07-01); Apache-2.0; not archived or renamed. The collector found no OSV advisory for 0.38.1 and npm build provenance. The README documents --session <id> --restore, state save/load and --profile, which bear on the open session-recovery gap but have not been measured. It documents no Lightpanda or alternate-engine option.
(2) alphaXiv/OpenResearch: pin 0.2.7 (2026-09-21) is five releases behind v0.2.12 (2026-09-28). Releases 0.2.8 to 0.2.12 shipped 09-22 to 09-28 with install-boilerplate bodies, so what changed is not stated. Latest main commit 7cc3251d91ec on 2026-09-29; MIT. Its README calls it 'The local-first workspace for research agents and autoresearch', installed by curl|sh, with 'orx up' opening a dashboard on 127.0.0.1:4791. It is therefore itself a standing research-agent workspace, in tension with this layer's requirement 'without another standing research-agent stack'. Its standing rests on incumbency (local_integration, conditional on linux, untested on macOS, no comparison).
(3) tavily-ai/tavily-cli: no GitHub release. The collector found PyPI tavily-cli 0.1.8 present, not yanked and with no OSV advisory, which verifies the pin's registry source. Whether 0.1.8 is the newest PyPI release was not established. Latest main commit fd745230e675 on 2026-09-16 (48 since 07-01); 19 stars. Its standing rests on incumbency: three small searches with one recorded miss, and an operator record of a 2026-09-26 user direction to make no new Tavily calls pending a free-arm bake-off.
(4) The microsoft/playwright-cli catalog pin, 0.1.21, is behind v0.1.22 (2026-09-28).
No winner is archived, renamed or relicensed.

INCUMBENCY. All three winners are local_integration, conditional on linux-wsl2 and untested on macos-arm64, with no measured comparison against any alternative.

NOT PROPOSED.
- exa-labs/exa-mcp-server (not adjudicated 09-26): its README says the hosted MCP at mcp.exa.ai 'works anonymously with rate limits', so a credential is not the blocker. It is maintained (latest main commit f3d71fb6b0ff on 2026-09-23; 27 since 07-01; no releases). It is not proposed because it adds a new third-party query processor, is MCP-only with no bounded shell command, and no native miss is recorded. Revisit as a compare arm if DDGS, SearXNG and native search all miss frozen targets.
- openai/codex (not adjudicated 09-26): its native web_search="live" is a baseline arm in the search bake-off, not a candidate.
- jina-ai/reader: excluded as stale. The REST commits?since=2026-07-01 check returned EMPTY; the last default-branch commit was 2026-05-22.
- KnockOutEZ/wigolo (707 commits since 07-01; v0.2.1; license NOASSERTION, information only) and D4Vinci/Scrapling (v0.4.15; 131 commits) were refuted 09-26 on returned votes. Both are maintained, and no new fit evidence was found this sweep.
- firecrawl/cli (refuted 09-26; v1.24.6), firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server (a 2025 v3.2.1 tag on an active branch, not stale) and firecrawl/firecrawl (self-host stack): hosted/keyed or a standing stack, with no gap beyond the proposed arms.
- browser-use/browser-use (0.13.10): an agent framework with hosted services, which conflicts with 'no standing research-agent stack'.
- ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp (v1.10.1, 2026-09-23): a DevTools MCP that overlaps agent-browser, with no retrieval gap.
- lightpanda-io/browser: a rolling 'nightly' tag on a very active branch (2205 commits since 07-01), so not stale. A non-Chromium engine would widen the open compatibility gap, and agent-browser's README documents no Lightpanda option.
- h4ckf0r0day/obscura (v0.2.3; created 2026-04-13) and citrolabs/ego-lite (v2.0.0; created 2026-04-16): browser runtimes over 90 days old, with no retrieval gap shown.
- brcrusoe72/agent-search (84 stars; 2 commits since 07-01; a SearXNG wrapper) and karust/openserp (v0.8.12; a browser-rendered SERP service): standing services covered by the SearXNG comparison.
- mozilla/readability (5 commits since 07-01): a library embedded in other extractors.
- eyuansu62/agent-retrieval-bench (from beyond_stars): its description reads 'Agentic code retrieval benchmark for coding agents', so it measures code rather than web retrieval and is not a baseline for this layer.
No seeded candidates were supplied.

VERIFICATION CAVEATS.
- The operator memory figure 'crawl4ai had 13 advisories, 7 critical' is not reproduced. The repository security-advisories endpoint lists 19 (5 critical, 11 high, 3 medium); the difference may come from the global advisory database versus the repository endpoint.
- Trafilatura's evaluation page cites Bevendorff et al. 2023 as 'Best single tool by ROUGE-LSum Mean F1'. Its webis.de link (bevendorff_2023b.pdf) resolves to a different paper ('SMAuC - The Scientific Multi-Authorship Corpus'), and the ACM PDF returned HTTP 403, so that external ranking is unverified at primary. A search snippet reports 'best overall mean performance (0.883)', but that is not primary.
- The collector's advisory coverage is direct packages only; the transitive tree was not examined.
- A prior-session context-mode record of a crawl4ai v0.9.4 review exists; it was treated as historical and not used as evidence.
- Third-party blog comparisons of agent-browser and playwright-cli (ytyng.com, test-lab.ai) are secondary and unreproduced.
- The ddgs CLI flags were read at HEAD, so the trial should pin v9.16.0.

CALLS.
- gh_api 34: one gh auth status, two GraphQL queries, 26 REST reads, and about 5 GitHub requests by the supply-chain-risk-auditor collector. The collector figure is inferred from one repository lookup per dependency, not observed, because its cache was not retained.
- The collector also made non-GitHub HTTP requests (15 fetched, 5 served from cache) to PyPI, npm, OSV and OpenSSF Scorecard, which are not counted as page fetches.
- web_fetch 6: four in one batch, one of which returned HTTP 403 (ACM); one context-mode fetch of the webis PDF, which indexed unreadable binary; one curl download of that PDF for pdftotext.

TOKEN TOOLS. ctx_execute and ctx_batch_execute were used for API and README output, ctx_fetch_and_index for pages and ctx_search to quote from them; no compressor was stacked.

output.notes:
Read-only assessment dated 2026-09-29. No candidates were installed or executed, and no credentials were read. Counts include failed requests; GitHub API requests are counted under gh_api without also counting them as page fetches. Research stopped at the eight-page fetch ceiling. Five general web-search queries returned no usable text. GitHub's core REST endpoints returned rate-limit errors; its separate repository-search API temporarily recovered metadata before also reaching its limit. Broad discovery and release coverage are consequently incomplete.

The 90-day cutoff is 2026-07-01. Required default-branch commit queries failed for all four proposed alternatives. No repository was excluded for unknown maintenance, and pushed_at was never treated as default-branch activity. Creation dates establish that Playwright CLI and Trafilatura are older than 90 days; repository age remains unverified for Crawl4AI and Scrapling. Null fields represent unavailable facts, including exact stars where pages only showed rounded counts. No dependency/advisory audit or model evaluation was performed.

Winner health: GitHub search API results retain the canonical names, report archived=false, and show the supplied licenses for [agent-browser](https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=agent-browser%20in%3Aname%20user%3Avercel-labs&sort=updated&order=desc&per_page=2), [Tavily CLI](https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=tavily-cli%20in%3Aname%20user%3Atavily-ai&sort=updated&order=desc&per_page=2), and [OpenResearch](https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=OpenResearch%20in%3Aname%20user%3AalphaXiv&sort=updated&order=desc&per_page=2). OpenResearch's pushed_at advanced to 2026-09-29T04:42:06Z, which is not proof of default-branch maintenance. Winner release tags were not independently revalidated; the supplied OpenResearch 0.2.7-to-v0.2.12 drift remains a follow-up. All three winners remain provisional controls: the supplied local-integration evidence does not establish comparative leadership, and no measured best was identified here.

Corrections and counterevidence: [Playwright's configuration documentation](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-cli#configuration-file) describes default file-URL blocking, so the recorded file-protocol rejection alone does not refute compatibility. [Agent-browser's current documentation](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser#tab-pinning) describes strict tab binding and recovery information; recovery is unmeasured in the retained fixtures, not established as absent. [Tavily's current README](https://github.com/tavily-ai/tavily-cli#non-interactive-mode-for-ai-agents--scripts) documents keyless search/extraction, while its authentication section records OAuth compatibility gaps. A blanket requirement for new credentials would therefore be unsupported. These current-branch statements still need installed-version and changelog checks before being attributed to the pinned clients.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The current path keeps no re-verifiable record of a cited page. ctx_fetch_and_index stores converted markdown with a 24 h default TTL and removes stored content older than 14 days (installed tool description). agent-browser 0.38.1 can save a HAR, a PDF and rendered text (README@v0.38.1 L145, L194-195, L371-374), but none of them records the TLS certificate chain or a provenance statement, and no layer receipt in the input shows them used as citation evidence. Scoop is a single-page 'witnessing the web' capture engine. It writes WARC, warc.gz or WACZ with a provenance summary and SSL-certificate attachments on by default, plus an optional PDF snapshot. It writes a JSON capture summary even for failed captures, uses an isolated browsing context per capture, and signs WACZ through an authsign-compatible endpoint. A trial is feasible now on the Linux workstation: Node v24.21.0 is present, npm engines require node>=22.0.0, and the README lists Linux, Mac OS and WSL. Caveats: (a) the README documents no page-text index, so quotes must be re-verified from the WARC payload or the PDF text; (b) the default provenance step calls icanhazip.com; (c) postinstall.sh downloads yt-dlp 2026.08.19 and crip 2.1.0 with pinned SHA-256, and on every Mac it fetches crip-macos-amd64 (Rosetta on M5 is unverified); (d) signing needs an authsign server, which is out of scope for a first trial.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Frozen set F: at least 30 URLs cited in this layer's receipts, plus JS-rendered docs pages, GitHub pages and one PDF, with one quote per URL taken at capture time. Add planted fabricated quotes as the negative control. Apply one normalization rule to every arm: entity decode, NFKC and whitespace collapse. Re-verify with the context-mode store purged and networking off (unshare -n). Report a loopback page edited after capture separately as a synthetic fixture. Control C0 needs no new install. It runs agent-browser 0.38.1 as network har start --content all, then open, get url, get text body and get html body, then pdf, then network har stop, with a sha256 manifest. For static pages it adds wget --warc-file (wget 1.21.4 on Linux; unverified on the Macs). Scoop 0.7.0 runs on F with --pdf-snapshot true, --json-summary-output, --public-ip-resolver-endpoint pointed at a loopback stub and video attachments off. Adopt Scoop only if all four hold: (1) it re-verifies at least as many true quotes as C0 from its archive and PDF alone; (2) it rejects every planted quote; (3) its WACZ datapackage.json resource hashes verify; (4) it adds provenance C0 lacks (certificate chain, provenance summary) at a per-page time and size the lane accepts. It is overturned if C0 matches (1) and (2) and the frozen citation checks do not require the extra provenance.

With --text to-pages the pages.jsonl text field carries the page text, and with --text final-to-warc the WARC carries post-behavior text as urn:textFinal:<url>. A cited quote can then be re-verified with unzip and grep and no network. It also writes CDXJ indexes, and linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 images are published. proposed.demonstrated_gap: Created 2026-06-30 (91 days, assessable). Headroom's native benefit is unestablished: interception of agent traffic is not configured and its native ledger saw zero calls. Chisle compresses tool output with no proxy, through the Claude Code PostToolUse hook. The current hooks reference says `updatedToolOutput` 'Replaces the tool's output with the provided value before it is sent to Claude' for all tools, not only MCP. That reaches outputs RTK's command rewriting cannot: Agent (subagent results), MCP, WebFetch/WebSearch and Grep/Glob. It keeps native subscription sign-in, and because it touches only new tool output, the cache prefix is never rewritten. It never touches Read/Edit. Elided middles spill to disk for targeted recovery (newest 40 kept). Every tier has an off switch. Its input-axis counter (chars actually elided) is kept separate from output-axis A/B arms, which matches this layer's artifact-versus-provider split. Native OTel tool spans record the original output before the hook runs, which gives an uncompressed baseline beside api_request billing. Limits: its own CHANGELOG for 3.0.0 (2026-07-28) records that before the fix the hook 'reported savings, and the model still received the full output', because Claude Code rejects a string for Bash's object-shaped output. The current code rebuilds the shape and 'skips shapes it cannot rebuild', so per-tool coverage is unproven. Evidence is a counterfactual 171-session replay (about 46% off eligible outputs, artifact class; dedup 0 hits) and one 6-task, single-run Pi A/B. There is no billed-cost or task-quality pairing on Claude Code. Its bundled prose and YAGNI rules (caveman/ponytail class) must be off for an input-axis trial.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Gate 1, per tool (Bash, Agent, Grep, WebFetch, MCP): the session transcript shows the compressed output while OTel tool_result result_tokens shows the original. Otherwise the ledger is unproven, as before 3.0.0. Then a frozen task set on both hosts, repeated with randomized order, comparing Chisle input axis only against headroom v0.39.1 and no compression. Measure task success; complete provider use from OTel api_request (input, output, cache_read and cache_creation per query_source, subagents included) plus api_error/api_retries_exhausted; turns; spill-file recoveries. Adopt only if success is non-inferior and billed-equivalent usage falls. Reject if recovery fails or extra turns erase the saving, which is the RTK pattern.

The team's own cost study calls tool-schema filtering 'the only lever that is unambiguously and reproducibly positive' (about 21K–57K tokens per turn), finds content compression saves '~2% of the (cache-priced) prefix per turn', and says single-shot benchmarks are 'orthogonal to multi-turn cost'. Self-host is the default (Ollama about 2.5 GB, or vLLM serving the LoRA over Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 on a 24 GB GPU), so only the linux RTX 4090 host is clearly feasible. A local proxy that records each request/response pair with input, output, cache-read and cache-creation usage. It redacts common auth headers but stores full prompts and tool results locally. I did not read the api_error attribute list; the doc's 'final api_error' wording implies one event per failed attempt without stating it. claude-tap's remaining value is as a trial instrument: adjacent-request diffs show what a gateway actually sent and whether the cache prefix stayed stable.

- graykode/abtop is a monitor; zilliztech/claude-context belongs to the code-retrieval layer. Green-PT/honey-for-devs, alexgreensh/attention-span and Kulaxyz/token-diet are caveman-class style skills. jia-gao/leanctx targets production LLM apps, not coding agents. ww-w-ai/super-token-saver surfaced in search but was not assessed. yvgude/lean-ctx: the 09-26 verdict stands; not rechecked.

NATIVE FACTS FOR THIS LAYER:
- PostToolUse updatedToolOutput replaces a result only when the value matches the tool's output schema; a mismatch is silently ignored. Chisle's own pre-3.0.0 ledger counted savings that never reached the model for exactly this reason.
- OTel tool spans capture the original output before the hook runs, so OTel tool_result result_tokens is a native pre-compression baseline for post-hoc compressors. It is not a baseline for PreToolUse command rewriters such as RTK and sqz.
- Paritok's own study ranks tool-schema filtering first. In this session MCP schemas are deferred until ToolSearch (an in-session observation; built-in schemas are still sent).

UNVERIFIED:
- native subscription sign-in through Paritok's base-URL proxy
- per-tool shape coverage of Chisle's rebuildResponse
- whether cost-bench separates cache buckets for Claude Code and supports repeated arms
- sqz's claim that it never invalidates prompt caches

TRIAL HYGIENE:
- sqz: run `sqz init` project-scoped (never --global), limited with --only to Claude Code, in an isolated HOME. Its init writes hooks, MCP config and agent guidance into every client it detects.
- cost-bench: use native logins and `run.sh --no-save-keys`.

METHOD:
- The McNemar p-value (0.0789 on 47 discordant pairs) was recomputed locally.
- supply-chain-risk-auditor was applied only as reading rules: unassessable is not risk, and repository contributor data are not publish rights. Its collector was not run (read-only lane, bounded budget), so no registry-level maintainer or advisory measurement exists for any candidate.
- Every quote comes from a 2026-09-29 fetch. The shared index also holds READMEs another session read on 09-27 (sqz, Paritok, agentacct, snip, llmtrim, claude-tap, loongsuite-pilot); none has a verdict on origin/main.
- Token tools used: ctx_execute and ctx_batch_execute to index GitHub API output, and ctx_fetch_and_index with ctx_search for pages.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: None of the winners (rtk, headroom, ccusage) reduces MCP tool-definition tokens. Native deferral already covers the default routes. (a) Claude Code on the first-party route defers every MCP tool. A historical receipt (v2.1.278, 2026-09-21) shows 'MCP tools: 609 tokens (0.1%)' with 92 tools from 6 servers deferred, and this lane's own subagent lists 111 MCP tools from 8 servers as names only. (b) By source, Codex rust-v0.158.0 defers MCP tools behind tool_search when the model's catalog entry has supports_search_tool (true for gpt-6-astra and gpt-6-sol in the bundled models.json) and the provider keeps namespace_tools (default true for configured providers). This is expected from source and was not observed on the OmniRoute lane. The gap is the eager route. On the repository's documented OmniRoute ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL route, Claude Code turns tool search off and loads every MCP tool schema upfront into the cached prefix. Subagents share that process environment. The native override ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true makes requests fail on proxies that do not support tool_reference blocks. Whether OmniRoute forwards them is unknown: a code search found no tool_reference handling, but a pass-through proxy need not name the blocks, so this is no evidence either way. mcp-compressor replaces a server's tool list with get_tool_schema and invoke_tool (list_tools is added at max) plus a compressed listing. The default level, medium, lists name(args) and the description's first sentence. The full schema is returned on demand, which fits this layer's recoverable-originals requirement. Secondary hypothesis: Codex's native deferral has two upstream issues open (#21503, exact-name misses; #34719, loss after compaction), neither reproduced at 0.158.0 by this lane, and a direct compressed listing might avoid them. Codex's native tool_input_schema_max_bytes (default 5,000 bytes) compacts large schemas; whether the model can recover the uncompacted schema is unverified. The vendor's figures are unverified: a 70-97% reduction and 'almost no impact' on quality in an unpublished evaluation. How often the OmniRoute Claude route is used is unknown.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Use a frozen task set of 20-30 prompts, each needing one named tool across the 8 configured servers, including exact-name requests and one turn after compaction. Draw prompts from MCP-Atlas where its tools overlap; otherwise freeze and record them. Run the prompts through the project's recorded upstream harness mapping (promptfoo, Inspect or Harbor), not a self-written runner. Use a fixed model, at least 3 repeats per arm, and keep failed attempts. Measure per arm: (1) upfront definition cost, counted three ways: the Claude /context 'MCP tools' row (loaded schemas), the deferred-names listing, and the MCP server-instructions block. Per subagent, use first-turn input tokens from the subagent transcript's usage, since /context is unavailable there. Per Codex session, use the first token_count event with the servers enabled minus disabled. (2) Complete provider usage per task, kept separate from cache subsets. (3) Tool-selection accuracy (the first call names the correct backend tool) and task success. (4) Recovery: the get_tool_schema output equals the backend tools/list schema. Arms: Claude first-party native deferral (control); Claude via OmniRoute at its default (eager); Claude via OmniRoute with ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true (the native fix, run first); Claude via OmniRoute plus mcp-compressor at medium and at high; and Codex 0.158.0 native deferral versus an mcp-compressor server with omit_tools_from=["deferred"]. Keep TOON output conversion off, and exclude --cli-mode, Code Mode, mcporter and mcp2cli, so definition savings are not counted twice with the MCP-to-CLI route or with output compressors. The trial fails whatever the savings unless all of these hold: Claude permission deny rules and PreToolUse hook matchers keyed on mcp__server__tool (context-mode routing, secret guard) still fire; Codex per-tool approval modes still apply; invoke-rate counting still resolves backend tool names; and backend server instructions (for example ai-memory's untrusted-memory guidance) still reach the model. Adopt for a route only if complete provider use drops at equal or better selection accuracy, every gate passes, and native deferral does not work on that route. Reject wherever native deferral works, since the proxy then only adds a hop and a schema round trip.

SCOPE: follow-up on the tool-definition share of context.

(1) Does Codex rust-v0.158.0 (2026-09-28) defer MCP tool schemas? Yes, by source. It defers them behind tool_search whenever model_info.supports_search_tool and the provider's namespace_tools both hold (spec_plan.rs 246-266 and 653-666).
- supports_search_tool is true for all 10 bundled models, including gpt-6-astra and gpt-6-sol.
- namespace_tools defaults to true for configured providers such as [model_providers.omniroute].
- Unknown slugs get fallback metadata with supports_search_tool false, and their MCP tools load directly.
- Setting omit_tools_from=["deferred"] on a server forces direct exposure.
- tool_input_schema_max_bytes (default 5,000 bytes) natively compacts large input schemas.
- This was not observed at runtime on the OmniRoute lane. Model metadata can also come from model_catalog_json or a remote /models, and the gateway must pass the Responses tool_search/namespace tool types. OmniRoute's source handles tool_search in its Responses/Codex translators, but that behavior is unverified. If the gateway does not pass them, expect errors or missing tools, not eager loading.

(2) This lane did not measure the native baseline.
- The 609-token, 92-deferred-tool figure is historical: Claude Code v2.1.278, 2026-09-21, 6 servers.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: One open gap is still open: Promptfoo and Inspect AI have not been compared on the same frozen cases. The 2026-09-26 sweep proposed a 60-case comparison, but no run is retained. Inspect 0.3.264-0.3.272 (16-28 Sep 2026) has since added failure-preserving behavior that bears directly on this layer's negative-control and fresh-case requirements. (a) Empty or whitespace completions are now scored with reason="no_response", so a model that returned nothing is distinguishable from one that answered wrong (0.3.269). (b) Samples cut off by a cancellation that Inspect did not issue are recorded as sample errors instead of scored as completed (0.3.269). (c) eval_set tops up a dataset that has grown with stable sample ids by running only the new samples (0.3.270). That fits adding freshly labeled cases without rerunning or re-tuning on the old ones. (d) human_reviewer() lets an operator review a tool call together with its result (0.3.264). (e) `inspect score --scorer pkg/name` resolves @scanner functions from installed packages (0.3.266). Promptfoo's retained evidence (4 upstream pairs and a 2-assertion echo fixture) exercises none of these conditions. This establishes trial value, not superiority.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Extend the recorded 60-case plan. Run Promptfoo 0.123.1 and Inspect 0.3.272 on the same frozen, independently labeled semantic-advice/extraction cases: identical recorded outputs, identical mock tool responses and the same judge model. Inject wrong-ticker, look-ahead-date, missing-tool and grader-error mutations. Add two negative-control arms: empty output, and an externally cancelled sample. Inspect joins or replaces Promptfoo only if it (1) catches more injected mutations, or labels both control arms distinctly (no_response or sample error) where Promptfoo scores them as ordinary pass or fail, and (2) keeps per-sample logs that locate each failure. Then add 20 newly labeled cases and confirm that eval_set runs only those. If the two tools reach parity on detection and failure localization, Promptfoo stays and Inspect stays keep_but_compare.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The next_action asks for semantic advice to be judged on fresh, independently labeled cases without tuning on the eight-case diagnostic, keeping uncertain disagreements and a safe negative control. The layer's retained evidence contains no measurement of judge-versus-human agreement and no held-out split. Scout documents this workflow natively. Validation sets of human-labeled transcripts are compared against scanner results and reported as balanced accuracy, precision, recall and F1. Dev/test splits keep scanner-prompt iteration on dev and scoring on a holdout. Label-set and per-case predicate formats are supported, and Scout View sorts validated results for review. Scout reads Claude Code sessions directly through its claude_code() source and lists Harbor among its import sources. The with-skill and no-skill arms of real harness runs can therefore be judged from their transcripts without rerunning them. Boundary: no uncertain or abstain class is documented. Uncertain cases would need their own split, excluded by the split filter (untested). Scout is pre-1.0 (0.5.3); created 2025-09-07.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Build copies of with-skill and no-skill Claude Code sessions that are sanitized and scoped to this trial. Import them with claude_code(path=<explicit trial directory>), never with the default, which scans every project under ~/.claude/projects/. Label the same 60 fresh cases independently into dev and test splits, with an 'uncertain' split kept out of the metrics. Develop one advice-followed scanner on dev only, then score the test split. Adopt Scout as the semantic-advice judge lane only if two conditions hold. First, its test-split balanced accuracy and F1 exceed Promptfoo llm-rubric scored against the same labels on the same held-out cases. Second, the no-skill negative-control arm yields no advice-followed flags. Otherwise it adds nothing over the winner. Execution on either host is untested.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The gap is runtime enforcement of action pins, not transitive coverage. All 13 distinct actions in the 20 workflows are SHA-pinned, and the repository's Actions policy reports sha_pinning_required: true. zizmor's online impostor-commit audit checks, statically at PR time, whether a pinned commit belongs to the repository itself or only to its fork network. Nothing enforces at run time that a locked commit sits on a branch of the named repository or that the repository identity has not been redirected. gh-actions-lock is GitHub's technical-preview extension for Workflow Dependency Pinning. It writes .github/workflows/actions.lock and, for onboarded workflows, blocks at run time any unlocked dependency, forged lock entry, commit not reachable from a branch, or repository redirect. It gives no transitive benefit here today: 12 of the 13 actions are node24 actions with no nested uses, none is composite, and there are no local actions. The one docker action, ossf/scorecard-action, runs docker://ghcr.io/ossf/scorecard-action:v2.4.4 by tag, and lock coverage of that image is unverified. Two things block it. Dependabot's weekly github-actions PRs are expected to change workflow SHAs without updating actions.lock until the announced Dependabot integration ships (not observed), which would split ownership of the same pins. The public-preview roadmap item github/roadmap#1253 is still open, so enforcement on Free public repositories is unconfirmed.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: On a throwaway branch, onboard all 20 workflows with gh-actions-lock pinned to v0.1.6 (or the release current at trial time) and run them hosted. Promote to targeted_candidate only if all of the following hold. (1) The runner enforces the lock on this Free public repository without preview enrollment. (2) A lock entry with a mutated SHA, an impostor fork-network commit and a renamed-repository redirect each stop the run before any job starts. (3) A Dependabot github-actions PR on the onboarded branch either updates actions.lock or fails visibly. Stay deferred while any of these fails. The baseline is zizmor 1.30.1's online impostor-commit audit plus the sha_pinning_required policy on the same commit.

It states 'Workflows that are onboarded to the lockfile enforce that all dependencies are present in the lockfile and guarantees that the locked commit for an Action is what's executed on the runner' and 'Repository identity is recorded and redirects and mismatches are blocked at runtime'. Locked commits must exist on a branch, and local-path actions are skipped.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Install-time known-malware blocking for host and agent-run installs. No running control covers this axis. The incumbents act in CI on committed files only: osv-scanner v2.6.0 (security-scan.yml) matches committed lockfiles against OSV, which carries OpenSSF MAL- records; dependency-review-action v5.0.0 gates PR diffs; harden-runner v2.21.1 audits egress without blocking. Host installs have no lockfile to scan: npm -g installs without a shrinkwrap, uv tool installs whose transitive PyPI dependencies are unlocked, the upstream launcher 'npx -y --prefer-online socraticode@latest' (docs/token-efficiency-stack.json:2978) and 'uvx --from git+...serena@c6fbd1c' (docs/foundation-stack.md:115). safe-chain wraps npm, npx, yarn, pnpm, pnpx, bun, bunx, pip, pip3, uv, uvx, poetry, pipx and pdm through a local proxy. It needs no token or account. Its README states that no build data is shared; this is a vendor claim, and its egress has not been observed. The malware database is bulk JSON (malware_predictions.json and malware_pypi.json from malware-list.aikido.dev), and a mirror can serve it (malwareListBaseUrl). A trial can therefore pin it by snapshot hash, which the layer's overturn_when requires. The 1.5.21 linux-x64 binary carries a GitHub in-toto attestation, so its provenance can be verified, unlike the checksum-only Syft install. Its 48-hour age gate adds nothing over a configured 7-day native cooldown: npm min-release-age exists since npm 11.10.0, and a user-level uv.toml exclude-newer duration governs uv tool and uvx. The 48-hour gate is also shorter than windows such as tj-actions (about 3 days) and Kong (about 10 days) in Woodruff's sample. The increment to test is therefore the denylist alone. It matters for installs made after a feed flags a version whose attack window outlasts the cooldown, and for installs that bypass the cooldown. TLS interception with an injected CA bundle (registryProxy/certBundle.js, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS) is inferred from source paths only; the code was not read.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Isolate the denylist from the age gate. (1) Offline and read-only first: hash a snapshot of Aikido's malware_predictions.json and malware_pypi.json, then diff it against the OSV MAL- records (ossf/malicious-packages) for npm and PyPI incidents of the last 90 days, comparing presence and first-seen time. If Aikido's entries are a subset of OSV MAL with no lead time, the incumbent replicates the blocker: resolve a lock or SBOM, run osv-scanner v2.6.0, then install. That result overturns this proposal. (2) Bounded host trial on linux-wsl2, then macos-arm64, in a scratch HOME with the --ci PATH shims and no rc-file edits. Verify the binary with 'gh attestation verify'. Set the age gate to 0 against native npm min-release-age=7 and a user-level uv.toml exclude-newer = '7 days'. Replay the stack's real install set in non-interactive shells: the bootstrap pins, uv tool installs, and the npx socraticode and uvx serena launches. Any of the following overturns it: a false block, a broken sha256-pinned or --ignore-scripts install, a CA bundle that leaks beyond the wrapped subprocess, or egress other than the registries and malware-list.aikido.dev. The vendor test packages safe-chain-test and safe-chain-pi-test prove the plumbing only, not detection quality. (3) Scope: host and ad-hoc installs only. Committed lockfiles stay with osv-scanner, so no dependency has two owners.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Install-script confinement, an axis nothing in the stack covers. PMG has an opt-in OS-native sandbox for installs: macOS Seatbelt, Linux Landlock, and Bubblewrap as fallback. The stack sometimes has to run lifecycle scripts. bootstrap-macos.sh:768 runs 'npm rebuild --ignore-scripts=false' after sha256-verifying the dependency. adoption/lifecycle.md:121 notes that a blanket --ignore-scripts can omit required native binaries. Neither a cooldown nor a denylist confines a script once it runs. PMG covers npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, npx, pnpx, pip, pipx, poetry, uv and uvx and needs no account or API key. It also has a configurable dependency cooldown (dependency_cooldown.days) and reproducible builds with GitHub and npm attestations. On the blocking axis it loses to safe-chain under this layer's overturn_when (pinned database, privacy). Each install is checked live against SafeDep's community API, so package names and versions leave the host. docs/config.md shows no offline or snapshot mode, so the database cannot be pinned; docs/caching.md was not read. Anonymous usage telemetry is on by default, with an opt-out (PMG_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true). HTTPS inspection uses a PMG CA (docs/cert.md, not read). Keep it for the sandbox axis, not as the blocker.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Promote to targeted_candidate when two conditions hold. First, the stack shows an unverified install that needs its scripts: --ignore-scripts breaks the tool, and the content is not sha256-pinned. Second, with telemetry disabled, a PMG sandboxed install on macOS Seatbelt (M5 Pro) or Linux Landlock (the WSL2 6.18 kernel, with Bubblewrap as fallback) completes that install, and it denies a planted write outside the install prefix and a planted read of a credential-store path. Landlock enablement on WSL2 is unverified. On the blocking axis, use the OSV-MAL incident set from the safe-chain trial. SafeDep's first-flag times would need a measurable lead over both OSV MAL and Aikido's snapshot to justify a live-API dependency with no pinned database.

RUNNING CONTROLS, RECORDED AS INCUMBENTS (not as candidates). GraphQL resolved every pin to its upstream tag on 2026-09-29, and each equals the latest release.
- ossf/scorecard-action is pinned at 2d1146689b8c, which is v2.4.4 (published 2026-07-23). scorecard.yml#L41-L45 runs it weekly, report-only (publish_results: false). The upstream default branch has 14 commits since 2026-07-01, the last on 2026-08-08: maintained, with low activity. Its 09-26 not_adopted rejection as a gate still holds.
- actions/dependency-review-action is pinned at a1d282b36b6f, which is v5.0.0 (published 2026-05-08). It runs with fail-on-severity: high (dependency-review.yml#L35-L37).
- step-security/harden-runner is pinned at e14015d58371, which is v2.21.1 (published 2026-08-30). Every hardened job uses egress-policy: audit. catalogs/foundation/automation.json says block mode needs a per-job allow-list backed by several audit runs.
- google/osv-scanner v2.6.0 (published 2026-09-14) is a sha256-checked download in security-scan.yml and scans the committed lockfiles listed in .github/osv-scanner-lockfiles.json. OSV carries OpenSSF MAL- records (OpenSSF blog, 2026-05-20), so this incumbent already flags known-malicious versions in committed lockfiles, but only at CI time.
- Dependabot updates github-actions only, weekly, with a cooldown of default-days 7.
- No running control has been compared on install-time blocking, so its standing on that axis rests on incumbency, not measurement. harden-runner in audit mode blocks nothing. Whether dependency-review surfaces GitHub malware advisories was not verified.

WINNER HEALTH (no archived, renamed or relicensed repository, and no major release):
- zizmor v1.30.1 equals the latest release; 153 commits since July.
- syft v1.52.0 equals the latest release; 182 commits since July.
- actions/attest is SHA-pinned at 1e69f48acb82, which is v4.2.2 (latest, 2026-08-04), in publish-catalog.yml at lines 126, 133 and 240. The layer input says 'unpinned', which is an input discrepancy.
- All three winners are native_proven on their own axes; none addresses blocking at package install.

NATIVE BASELINE THE BLOCKERS MUST BEAT; CONFIGURE IT FIRST.
- npm min-release-age (in days) arrived in npm v11.10.0 on 2026-02-11 (npm/cli#8965). It is unset everywhere in the repo; the only hit is a quoted cdxgen install line in catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260926.json. The docs read do not say whether npx (npm exec) honours it; unverified.
- pnpm 11 defaults to minimumReleaseAge 1440, blockExoticSubdeps true and strictDepBuilds true. The repo fixture uses pnpm 12.4.2. The 12.0.0 release-note lines I read do not reverse those defaults; nothing further was verified.
- uv accepts duration values for exclude-newer since PR #16814, merged 2025-12-09. Issue #18829 (UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER durations) closed 2026-04-02. uv tool commands read only user-level and system-level uv.toml, so a user-level setting covers uvx and uv tool. The repo uses only a fixed --exclude-newer timestamp, at hardware-profile-smoke.yml#L95.
- --ignore-scripts applies only to pins flagged ignore_scripts (bootstrap-linux.sh#L293-L307) and to the pnpm fixture.
- In Woodruff's sample, 8 of 10 attacks had windows shorter than one week.
- Recommended order:
  1. Set 7-day native cooldowns on both hosts: .npmrc min-release-age=7, user-level uv.toml exclude-newer = '7 days', and pnpm minimumReleaseAge 10080 where pnpm is used.
  2. Run the offline diff of the Aikido lists against OSV MAL.
  3. Run the safe-chain host trial only if that diff shows entries or lead time that OSV MAL lacks.

SEEDED CANDIDATES AND STARS
- The layer input has seeded_candidates: []. The critic named two items, and both were checked: safe-chain is proposed; sfw-free is rejected on the maintenance rule, as a release-only repository.
- Stars scan: no item among the 357 star_candidates or 102 beyond_stars covers package blocking at install. The CI-adjacent items (gitleaks, trivy, cosign, awesome-actions) are already covered or overlap.

NOT PROPOSED
- ossf/malicious-packages is maintained (1994 commits since July), but it is the data source for the overturn diff, not a tool.
- SocketDev/action (firewall-free mode) and SocketDev/sfw-installer only wrap sfw.

UNVERIFIED
- One search found no independent detection benchmark; the only comparisons are vendor-written, such as the PMG README table.
- safe-chain: the 'no build data shared' claim, and whether its CA bundle stays within the wrapped subprocess.
- Whether Landlock is enabled on the WSL2 kernel.
- PMG docs/caching.md and docs/cert.md were not read.
- The pnpm 12 defaults beyond the 12.0.0 lines read.

HOST CONSTRAINTS FOR ANY TRIAL
- Use a scratch HOME and PATH shims only. Host deny rules protect ~/.profile, .bashrc and .zshrc, and shell aliases do not fire in non-interactive agent shells.
- Observe egress during the trial.
- Set PMG_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true if PMG is ever run.

SKILLS AND TOKEN TOOLS
- search-first.
- supply-chain-risk-auditor: its principles only. Its collector was not run, because it audits a project's manifests, not candidate tools.
- fp-check: applied to the sfw-free and SCFW rejections and to safe-chain's no-data claim.
- Token tools: context-mode ctx_batch_execute, ctx_fetch_and_index and ctx_search for READMEs and docs; GraphQL batching for metadata; no compressor stacking.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The winner's own open recovery case, which configuration can now test. Under the 2026-09-23 preregistered SIGKILL protocol (150 s bound, no scheduler), Dagu 2.16.6 failed: retries were refused for the whole bound. A post-hoc scheduler variant recovered in 181.4 s and 182.6 s. Temporal passed at 15 s, but with a tuned 5 s heartbeat timeout, and the record states the recovery setups 'were not equivalent'. Dagu's configuration reference makes stale-run detection tunable, with defaults proc.stale_threshold 90s, scheduler.zombie_detection_interval 45s and scheduler.failure_threshold 3 ('Consecutive stale checks before marking a run as failed'). Those defaults are arithmetically consistent with the ~182 s (90 s plus two or three 45 s checks), but the cause is not proven. Proc liveness 'appl[ies] to all locally owned DAG runs', yet zombie detection is a scheduler setting, so the no-scheduler protocol left the killed run in running state (inference from the reference plus the failed run). The pin is also behind. v2.17.2 (2026-09-25) is latest. 2.17.0's recovery-relevant fixes (#2775 'stop dropping queued retries', #2809 'wait for durable status before continuing past a node') have only a graceful stop/retry parity receipt, and SIGKILL was not re-run. 2.17.2 adds #2838 (resume independent branches while tasks wait), #2847 (replace stdout/stderr artifact per attempt) and dagu start --only (#2855). A matched, tuned SIGKILL run is a bounded native trial on both hosts, and it decides whether any durable challenger is needed for single-host crash recovery. Cross-host worker loss stays uncovered because issue #2805 (recovery after distributed worker loss) is open.

(b) Tuned settings, for example proc.heartbeat_interval 2s and heartbeat_sync_interval 2s (both well below proc.stale_threshold 15s), scheduler.zombie_detection_interval 5s and failure_threshold 2.
(c) The retained Temporal arm with its 5 s heartbeat timeout.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Among self-contained server binaries, Restate is the only surveyed engine that addresses loss of the server host itself, not just a worker (open gap 1). Its cluster docs say that running at least 2*default-replication-1 nodes tolerates default-replication-1 node failures, and 2n+1 metadata-server nodes tolerate n metadata failures. So the WSL2 workstation plus both Macs (3 nodes, replication 2) could lose any one host. None of the other candidates does this without replicating an external database: Temporal's dev server keeps state in one SQLite file, Dagu relies on one coordinator, DBOS and Absurd rely on one Postgres, and Conductor and Kestra (HA is Enterprise-only) reach it only through replicated external backends. v1.7.12 (2026-09-22) ships restate-server for aarch64-apple-darwin and x86_64-unknown-linux-musl. The 2026-09-26 sweep refuted it only through the GPT-6 fit vote's license veto ('a policy exclusion'), while the Claude fit vote kept it. With licenses now information only, that refutation does not stand on merit. It is compare, not trial, for four reasons. It was never executed on the frozen cases ('Dagster and Restate were not executed'). No real job has shown it needs to survive server-host loss (paper runs are one-shot systemd-run units with Restart=no). The docs carry operating cost: replacing a node needs a snapshot repository (object store or manual filesystem export), and 'If you have lost all nodes which previously hosted this partition, you have permanent data loss'. And there is an unverified WSL2 risk: the Macs must reach the workstation node inbound, which needs mirrored networking or a port proxy. Process-tree cancellation would also need handler adapter code, as with Temporal.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Port compare.py's four frozen cases to a Restate Python service adapter. Carry the fixture checkpoint as a journaled step result or keep the work directory on a shared mount. Form a 3-node cluster (WSL2 plus both Macs, replication 2, snapshot repository configured) and kill the node leading the finalize invocation's partition mid-finalize.
Restate passes if a surviving node completes within 150 s with checkpoint reuse, no duplicate completed.json and zero descendants on every host, and a cancel bounds the subprocess tree. Record node processes, setup steps and snapshot-store burden against Temporal's single-server arm.
A pass plus a real job that must survive server-host loss makes Restate the targeted challenger. It becomes not_adopted if the cluster cannot form across WSL2 and macOS or fails the kill case.
